headline: All majors below the 200-day line, momentum flat, but whales hauling ETH to cold storage while stablecoins pile on exchanges.
paragraphs: The regime is underwater across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Ripple, Binance Coin, Dogecoin, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have printed a golden cross. This is a bear market structure by the textbook definition. Bitcoin sits 49 percent below its 12-month high of $124,773, Ethereum 60.6 percent below $4,829, and Solana the worst of the major seven at 70.4 percent underwater. The 30-day realized volatility tells the story of a market in distress: Cardano at 73 percent, Ethereum at 45.4 percent, and Solana at 42 percent all indicate the tape is jittery. Over the last seven days, Bitcoin has lost 1.59 percent, Solana has dropped 4.01 percent, and Dogecoin has fallen 2.68 percent. Only Ethereum and Cardano have printed small green candles over the week (1.81 and 0.21 percent, respectively), but neither momentum nor trend supports them.

The momentum picture is muddy and offers no rescue. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, neutral and uninformative. Ethereum at 56.3 is in the upper neutral band but MACD is below signal, meaning the recent pop (up 6.36 percent on the month) is not backed by accelerating momentum. Solana at 42.7 and Cardano at 46.1 are both in weak territory, while Ripple and Dogecoin are even softer at 42.9 and 40.7 respectively. Only Binance Coin and Dogecoin have MACD above signal line, but neither is paired with price above the 200-day, so these are corrective bounces in a downtrend, not regime shifts. The contradiction worth naming: Ethereum is the month's relative outperformer (up 6.36 percent since July 24) yet remains below its trend line and its momentum is fading. This is a setup that often precedes reversal.

Derivatives positioning shows two separate narratives. On Bitcoin and Ethereum, funding is moderate (7.2 and 11.0 percent annualized, respectively) and the long-to-short ratio is balanced (1.0 and 1.18). Open interest on BTC is $2.31 billion and on ETH is $1.47 billion, healthy size but not stretched. Liquidations over the last eight hours skew long: Bitcoin saw $7.28 million in long liquidations versus $5.51 million short, and Ethereum was starker with $10.82 million long liquidations to $4.83 million short. This suggests weak hands on the bid are being flushed. However, the smaller alts tell a different story. Solana has a long-to-short ratio of 1.9, Ripple 2.11, and Dogecoin 3.56, meaning retail and smaller traders are heavily skewed long and crowded. Funding on these is 11 percent annualized (SOL, XRP) and 5.2 percent (DOGE), which is paying but not expensive. The risk is concentrated in the long side of the alt complex: if price breaks lower, the liquidation cascade will be asymmetric.

Whale flows are the day's most actionable tension. Over the last 24 hours, $110.8 million net moved off exchanges, which sounds bullish until you disaggregate it. Ethereum had zero inflows and $146 million in outflows, a clear cold-storage move. Bitcoin, by contrast, had $152.9 million inflow to $117.7 million outflow, netting $35.2 million coming onto exchanges (primarily to OKEx). The biggest single move: $146 million in ETH leaving Binance. This is textbook accumulation by whales, not panic. But here is the counter-signal: over the same 24 hours, $136.5 million in USDC and $100 million in USDT moved onto Binance. Stablecoin float is $308.6 billion, essentially flat on the month (up 0.02 percent), which means dry powder is not accumulating. The weekly flow cadence is telling: week of August 3rd saw $1.075 billion move off exchanges (strong accumulation), but the last three weeks (August 10, 17, and 24) have each seen money flow back onto exchanges, with the week ending August 24 at a net $802 million onto exchanges. This is a reversal of the accumulation trend. Whales are moving Ethereum to custody while tightening their grip on stablecoins; traditional finance (ETF flows) is still bid (BTC +$307.5M and ETH +$184M on August 21, both with five consecutive days of inflow), but the weekly whale pattern has turned. This disagreement between TradFi inflow and crypto whale redistribution is the session's key tension.

The Fear and Greed Index stands at 73, in 'Greed' territory, with a 30-day range of 25 to 73. The gauge has swung from deep fear to greed in a single month, yet the tape has not followed: Bitcoin is down 2.97 percent on the month, Ethereum up 6.36 percent, and Solana flat. The crowd is euphoric, but price is not confirming, and the momentum divergence (MACD below signal on five of seven majors) suggests the sentiment is ahead of the technicals. Total market cap dropped 0.67 percent in the last 24 hours even as the fear gauge points to crowd conviction. Bitcoin dominance is 59.1 percent, down from recent highs and stable, meaning altcoins have neither collapsed nor surged relative to Bitcoin.

Watch for three conditions: (1) whether Bitcoin and Ethereum can reclaim the 200-day moving average in the next session or two, which would suggest the bear structure is breaking; (2) whether the weekly whale flows reverse again toward off-exchange accumulation, signaling renewed institutional bid; and (3) whether MACD crosses above signal on the alts, particularly Solana, where the long liquidation risk is highest. If all three remain negative, the structure remains a downtrend with a crowd that is ahead of the fundamentals. If two flip, there is a setup worth monitoring. Until then, the tape shows a market with disconnected buyers (TradFi, cold storage) and distributed sellers (on-chain liquidations, weekly flows back to exchanges).
